messages.subject: Multilevel SEM, level 2 model, standard errors are all NA..
parts:
Hi, I have conducted a daily diary study and my data consists of almost 110 individuals with 9 day observations each.

I have 1 predictor, 3 mediators, 1 outcome variable.

And I'm more interested in between-person level.

 

Q1. If I want to test level 2 only, what should I do?

I found an instruction about having level 1 model only (below) from your homepage but not sure how to do in my case.. 


(from https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/multilevel.html) 

if you do not have a model in mind for level 2, you can specify a saturated level by adding all variances and covariances of the endogenous variables (here: y1, y2 and y3):

model <- '

level: 1

fw =~ y1 + y2 + y3

fw ~ x1 + x2 + x3

level: 2

y1 ~~ y1 + y2 + y3

y2 ~~ y2 + y3 y3 ~~ y3

'



Q2.

The reason why I’m asking this question is because I got the following warning messages about all my within-person indicators for some individuals(clusters):

Level-1 variable “r1” has no variance within some clusters. The cluster ids with zero within variance are: A1, …

Level-1 variable “r2” has no variance within some clusters. The cluster ids with zero within variance are: A1, …  

…

And the summary(fit) printed standard errors which are all NA. 


Any help would be greatly appreciated, thanks!!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Multilevel SEM, level 2 model, standard errors are all NA..
parts:
Q1. If I want to test level 2 only, what should I do?

I found an instruction about having level 1 model only (below) from your homepage but not sure how to do in my case..

Do you have a multiple-indicator measurement model at level 2?  Since you measured it on several occasions, and your N is too small to use the standard longitudinal CFA (with occasions in wide format), you would need to specify the same measurement model at both levels, with equal factor loadings across levels.  This follows from the assumption that you are measuring the same person-level construct at each occasion.  See here for a discussion about this in the context of subjects nested in groups/clusters:

https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2017.01640/full

Q2. The reason why I’m asking this question is because I got the following warning messages about all my within-person indicators for some individuals(clusters):

Level-1 variable “r1” has no variance within some clusters. The cluster ids with zero within variance are: A1, …

Level-1 variable “r2” has no variance within some clusters. The cluster ids with zero within variance are: A1, …

It looks like those are constant within each subject whose cluster ID is listed in the message (A1, ...).  If they are constant within all subjects, then they are Level-2 variables only, so they should not appear in your Level-1 model.

Posting your syntax would make it easier to provide more informative advice.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.subject: Applying 1-(1,1)-1 (Preacher et al., 2010), multilevel mediation
parts:
Thanks for your response!

After I got your response I've studied more and changed my syntax.

Basically, I attempted to adopt and change 1-(1,1)-1 mediation syntax from Preacher, K. J., Zyphur, M. J., & Zhang, Z. (2010). A general multilevel SEM framework for assessing multilevel mediation. Psychological Methods, 15, 209-233.

Could you please check my syntax (below) and give me some comments? 


- Variables in my model.
1 IV
2 Mediators (M1, M2) 
1 DV
2 control variable (C1, C2) 
(Except C2, which is measured at level two, all other variables are measured at level 1(daily diary)).


model111b<-'
level:1
DV ~ e1*M1 + e2*M2 + e3*M3 + f*IV + C1 <- I want to control C1 for both direct and indirect effect. Am I doing right?
M1~d1*IV + C1 <- I want to control C1 for both direct and indirect effect. Am I doing right?
M2~d2*IV + C1
M3~d3*IV + C1 
M1~~M2 <-- Is it correct? or should I exclude it?
M2~~M3 <-- Is it correct? or should I exclude it?
M1~~M3 <-- Is it correct? or should I exclude it?

level:2
DV~ b1*M1 + b2*M2 + b3*M3 + c*IV + C1 + C2  <--Should I use group mean of M1,M2,M3,IV,C1? Currently, I put the same variable name used in the level 1 equation.
M1~a1*IV + C1 + C2
M2~a2*IV + C1 + C2
M3~a3*IV + C1 + C2
M1~~M2 <-- Is it correct? or should I exclude it?
M2~~M3 <-- Is it correct? or should I exclude it?
M1~~M3 <-- Is it correct? or should I exclude it?
#indirect and total effects between
ab1:=a1*b1
ab2:=a2*b2
ab3:=a3*b3 
totalbw:=ab1+ab2+ab3+c

#indirect and total effects within
de1:=d1*e1
de2:=d2*e2
de3:=d3*e3 
totalwith:=de1+de2+de3+f
'

fit111b<-sem(model111b,data=dataA,cluster="ID")
summary(fit111b,fit.measures=TRUE)



Thank you very much!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Applying 1-(1,1)-1 (Preacher et al., 2010), multilevel mediation
parts: - Variables in my model.

2 Mediators (M1, M2) 

Below, it looks like you have 3 mediators.

model111b<-'
level:1
DV ~ e1*M1 + e2*M2 + e3*M3 + f*IV + C1 <- I want to control C1 for both direct and indirect effect. Am I doing right?
M1~d1*IV + C1 <- I want to control C1 for both direct and indirect effect. Am I doing right?
M2~d2*IV + C1
M3~d3*IV + C1
You mean you want to estimate direct and indirect effects while controlling for C1?  Yes, you regress all endogenous variables on C1.  (same response about C1 and C2 in the Level 2 model)

M1~~M2 <-- Is it correct? or should I exclude it?
M2~~M3 <-- Is it correct? or should I exclude it?
M1~~M3 <-- Is it correct? or should I exclude it?
Yes, unless you have a reason to assume these only covary because of IV and C1.  Same response for Level 2 model.

level:2
DV~ b1*M1 + b2*M2 + b3*M3 + c*IV + C1 + C2  <--Should I use group mean of M1,M2,M3,IV,C1? Currently, I put the same variable name used in the level 1 equation.
Yes, use the variable names.  Only their level-2 components can be in the level-2 model.  That (latent) decomposition is a given.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
